root_cause.text: The incore log roundoff value (l_iclog_roundoff) was incorrectly defaulted to a fixed 512 bytes (BBSIZE) when no log stripe unit is present, ignoring the log sector size (sb_logsectsize) which can be larger (e.g., 4096), leading to misaligned log writes and corruption.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds an `else if (mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize > 0)` branch to use `mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize` as the roundoff value, instead of unconditionally falling back to `BBSIZE`. The CVE description and commit message explicitly describe the failure: on a filesystem with log sectsz=4096 and sunit=0, the roundoff value was 512, causing "Torn write (CRC failure)" and unmountable filesystems.

intent_record.intent_summary: Use sb_logsectsize as iclog roundoff if sb_logsunit is unavailable but sector size is positive, instead of always defaulting to BBSIZE.
intent_record.what: Added an else-if branch that sets log->l_iclog_roundoff to mp->m_sb.sb_logsectsize when sb_logsectsize > 0, between the existing condition for sb_logsunit and the fallback to BBSIZE.
intent_record.how: At runtime, when allocating the log, if the filesystem has logv2 and sb_logsunit > 1, roundoff uses sb_logsunit. Otherwise, now sb_logsectsize is considered: if greater than 0, roundoff uses that; else falls back to BBSIZE. This changes behavior for filesystems with a positive log sector size but without a logsunit value.

grouping_result.intent: Use sb_logsectsize as iclog roundoff if sb_logsunit is unavailable but sector size is positive, instead of always defaulting to BBSIZE.

relevance_review.reason: The group directly changes the default iclog roundoff value from BBSIZE to sb_logsectsize when log stripe unit is unavailable, which is the exact fix for the root cause described.

candidates.rationale: Always defaults to fixed 512 bytes (BBSIZE) when logsunit is not set, ignoring sb_logsectsize which can be larger, causing misaligned log writes.
Condition fails to consider sb_logsectsize, so when logsunit is absent or ≤1, it falls through to default BBSIZE instead of using the sector size.

vuln_statements.explanation: Directly defaults l_iclog_roundoff to a fixed 512 bytes (BBSIZE) when no log stripe unit is present, ignoring sb_logsectsize which can be larger, leading to misaligned log writes and corruption.
Condition fails to check sb_logsectsize, so when logsunit is absent or <=1, the code falls through to the vulnerable default of BBSIZE instead of using the sector size, preventing correct alignment.
